name: Facet
text: We should prioritize a dark theme for our interface because it provides better visibility and clarity, especially for data visualization. This decision is influenced by the success of similar dark-themed interfaces, such as Manus Competitive Analysis and Graphify Dashboard. By choosing a dark theme, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially higher development time to ensure sufficient contrast and readability. This investment is worthwhile because a well-designed dark theme can significantly enhance the liveliness and enjoyment of our screen.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes hurt readability for users with astigmatism or in bright environments—our screencasts will look washed out on YouTube. Test both themes with a 5-person usability sprint; if dark scores below 70% comprehension in 30 seconds, switch to a light theme with high-contrast accents.

name: Facet
text:
Choose a dark theme with a high-contrast accent color for key elements like graphs and interactive controls. This keeps the liveliness and clarity of dark interfaces while fixing the readability issues in bright environments—our screencasts will stay sharp on YouTube. The trade-off is slightly higher eye strain for users with astigmatism, but we mitigate it with a clean, spacious layout and optional light mode. Test both themes in the sprint; if comprehension drops below 70%, we’ll default to light mode.

name: Pane
text: Pane: High-contrast accents on a dark theme still fail users with astigmatism—bright yellow on black is a readability trap. Test a light theme with *one* saturated accent color instead; if comprehension drops below 70% in 30 seconds, we default to a clean light theme with no dark mode at all. That’s the only way to settle it.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a one-time first-launch theme picker (dark/light/system) and default to a light theme with a single saturated accent color for key elements. The result must deliver a clear, readable, and visually consistent interface that passes the 70% comprehension threshold in a 5-person usability sprint, owned by Pane.
